newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian stocks pull index past key 200 level.
newsitem.headline: Estonian stocks pull index past key 200 level.

text.p: Bullish Estonian shares moved past the key level of 200 on the stock exchange on Friday for the first time, supported by gains in leading share Hansapank and other banks.
Dealers said that buying of Estonian shares in Helsinki helped the market.
"There was good support for Hansapank and Union Bank shares again in Helsinki which flowed onto the Tallinn market pumping the market up," one dealer said.
The Tallinn stock exchange index gained 1.95 percent to close at 200.15 on a turnover of 49.2 million kroons on the official list.
"Crossing the 200 mark for the Talse is definitely psychologically important for the market," said Mart Meerits, a trader from Hansapank.
Hansapank was the market leader with a turnover of 18.6 million kroons of shares to close 3.60 kroons higher on 198.20.
During the day's trade, Hansapank set a new record with its price crossing the 200 kroons level but later fell back.
Hansapank closed 1.50 markka higher in Helsinki at 75 although volume was low at 400.
Union Bank firmed by 1.05 kroons to close on 41.90 with a trade of 5.9 million kroons. It ended 0.80 markka higher at 16 in Helsinki on volume of 1,000.
Savings Bank closed 2.60 kroons higher at 95.00 kroons with 10.8 million kroons of shares changing hands.
Forekspank registered a trade of 9.9 million kroons to end 1.60 kroons higher on 148.50 kroons.
Tallinna Pank again moved upwards to close 1.20 kroons higher on 61.75 kroons on a trade of 3.4 million kroons.
The over-the-counter market remained in the shadow of the main list with volume of only 6.7 million kroons.
Rakvere meat plant registered turnover of 2.25 million kroons to close 0.15 kroons weaker on 13.45 kroons.
Saku brewery turned over almost two million kroons of shares to close 0.50 kroons down at 50.00 kroons.
Norma plastics maker was slightly stronger on 58.20 kroons a rise of 0.20 kroons based on a trade of 1.9 million kroons of shares.
-- David Mardiste, Tallinn Newsroom, +372 630 8400 or reuters@reuters.ee
